Subject: Draft MAP + timing — Halcyon evaluation and commercial milestones

Neha / team,

Thanks again for the product demo last week — the team at Halcyon is excited about the latency profile and the cost controls you showed. We want to move from evaluation to a time-boxed Mutual Action Plan that ties key commercial milestones (pricing, commits, ramp) to the evaluation gates so Procurement and Finance can sign off.

Top-level asks from our side:
- A clear MAP with 6–8 week evaluation gates and success criteria (quality thresholds + perf).
- Proposed committed capacity and pricing tiers for a 12–month initial term.
- A transparent mechanism for renewal/expansion uplift if we exceed committed usage during year 1.

Can you share a draft MAP and an example uplift model/one-pager we can show Finance? We’d like to get an internal alignment call with Procurement on Friday (8/14) if possible.

Thanks,
Emma Stone
VP, Product Engineering
Halcyon Health

Subject: Re: Draft MAP + timing — Halcyon evaluation and commercial milestones

Emma — really appreciate the clear asks. I’ve pulled together a short MAP draft and a pricing sheet that maps milestones to commit bands and suggested discount ladders. Key highlights (see attached MAP_draft_v1.pdf and pricing_sheet_v3.xlsx):

- Evaluation plan: 8-week evaluation broken into two 4-week gates. Gate 1: integration + latency/throughput smoke tests. Gate 2: fidelity and scale (prefix caching + autoscaling test).
- Commercial milestones: start with a conservative committed band (S: 50k tokens/day, M: 200k, L: 600k). We proposed an initial 3% introductory discount on M and L if executed before demo+PPO.
- Ramp & uplift: for any month where actual usage > committed band by >25% we propose a 30-day notice and an uplift applied at renewal. For example, if Year 1 average monthly usage ends up 40% above committed, renewal pricing would rebase to the measured usage band with a 6–12% step-up depending on how quickly adoption accelerated.

I’m attaching a one-pager that explains the uplift mechanics (redwood_uplift_onepager.pdf) and a simple table in the pricing sheet showing applied uplift scenarios.

Next steps:
- I can join your Procurement call on Friday 8/14 at 10:00am PT if that works.
- If you’d like, we can propose a tracked DocuSign that captures the MAP milestones + provisional pricing so Procurement has something to review ahead of the call.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Date: Fri, 14 Aug 2026 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft MAP + timing — Halcyon evaluation and commercial milestones

Neha / Emma — quick note from the AE manager side: the approach looks good. A couple of suggestions before we lock the DocuSign.

1) Discount ladder refinement: instead of a flat 3% intro on M/L, propose a consumption-staircase: 0–2x committed -> base price, 2–4x -> +4% uplift on margin (we absorb some), >4x -> renegotiation trigger. It gives Halcyon predictable economics up to a point and a clear renegotiation pathway.
2) Renewal uplift mechanics: make the uplift applied only at contract renewal (not retroactive billing). That reduces procurement pushback. We can include a cap (e.g., max +12% effective price step per renewal) and a clause specifying how smoothing is applied if usage spikes mid-term.
3) Include a mutual opt-out delivery milestone at end of Gate 1 (if integration fails to meet perf thresholds). Keeps the evaluation low-risk for both sides.

If you want, I’ll draft the DocuSign with those clauses; otherwise we approve the MAP draft and will join Friday’s call.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Director, Strategic Accounts
ben_carter@redwood.com

Thanks — the team reviewed your MAP and Ben’s notes. Procurement is comfortable with applying any uplift at renewal (non-retroactive) and likes the cap idea. A couple of clarifying asks before we proceed to DocuSign: 

- Can you provide the one-pager in a more finance-friendly format that shows 3 renewal scenarios (flat usage, +30% sustained, +70% sustained) with the resulting renewal price and step-up numbers? Our CFO wants to see the modeled impact.
- Confirm that the mutual opt-out at Gate 1 will include a 7-day remediation window before either party may terminate.
- Please include a sample signature block in DocuSign that includes our SOW/PO reference number field; Procurement requires it.

If you can get the revised one-pager and a DocuSign preview by EOD Friday (9/3), we’ll aim to sign the provisional MAP and move to Gate 1 next week.

Appreciate the responsiveness.
Emma Stone
VP, Product Engineering
Halcyon Health
